Support the gallery

To keep our doors open & free to the public, we rely on the financial support from individuals, trusts and foundations to present an ambitious programme of exhibitions, screening, events and learning activities, in addition to the core funding from Arts Council England and Southwark Council.

There are many ways of supporting us; starting or building your own art collections by purchasing artworks or limited editions from our online shop, sponsoring a project, donations, or becoming a member of our supporter’s circle

What's on   //  Lake Gallery   //  Dilston Gallery   //  Outdoors

In Conversation with Isabel Nolan
some fundamental forces

  //   Lake Gallery  //  Dilston Gallery Time:   Friday 16 October, 4-5pm

Join us in conversation with Isabel Nolan and Southwark Park Galleries Director Judith Carlton on Friday 16 October, 4-5pm, across both sites of Nolan’s solo exhibition some fundamental forces at Lake and Dilston Galleries.

The first comprehensive solo exhibition of Irish artist Isabel Nolan’s work in the UK to date, the exhibitions interconnected themes emphasise what Nolan refers to as “the fraught, exciting and unreliable nature of making connections” by seeking encounters and intimacy with cultural forces, institutions or methodologies that tell us what it means to be human.  

Discussing works made over two decades, including painting, drawing, sculpture, photography, text and textiles, this walking in-conversation comes at a significant moment in Nolan’s career as she represents Ireland at the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia. 

The event begins at Southwark Park Galleries, Lake Gallery, followed by a guided walk to Dilston Gallery.

Tickets are free with an optional donation. Booking is required.

Book Tickets

Isabel Nolan (b. 1974, Dublin, Ireland; lives and works in Dublin, Ireland) 

Nolan is representing Ireland at the 61st International Art Exhibition- La Biennale di Venezia. Solo exhibitions: Château La Coste, Aix-en-Provence, France (2023); Void Gallery, Derry, Northern Ireland (2022); Solstice Arts Centre, Navan, Ireland (2021); Kunstverein Langenhagen, Germany (2018); London Mithraeum Bloomberg SPACE, London (2017); Douglas Hyde Gallery, Dublin (2017); Kunstverein Graz, Austria (2017); Contemporary Art Gallery, Vancouver; Mercer Union, Toronto, Canada (2016) and the Irish Museum of Modern Art, (2014).  Recently her work has also been exhibited at the 13th Liverpool Biennial (2025); , Salzburger Kunstverein, Austria (2021); and EVA International, Limerick (2018). Nolan is represented by Kerlin Gallery, Dublin and Sikkema, Malloy, Jenkins, NYC.   

@nolanisabel

Accessibility

  • Chairs are available on request, please note there will be walking inside galleries and between buildings.
  • Both galleries are step-free and toilet accessible. Please note the altar of Dilston is not wheelchair accessible.
  • For more accessibility information please see our Visit webpage.
